statements.text: Artificial intelligence is only going to make it easier for the government to do this, and harder to detect. This should not be a partisan issue. We must get to the bottom of how the Federal Government uses AI to violate the privacy and civil liberties of the American people before it is too late.
statements.context: Senator Paul delivers an opening statement at a Senate hearing on AI in government, warning that federal agencies are using AI for surveillance and censorship.

statements.text: The only way you could possibly get through that is with some kind of AI program.
statements.context: Senate hearing on Artificial Intelligence in Government, Senator Paul questioning witnesses about surveillance, disinformation, and free speech.

statements.text: I, for one, do not fear AI at all if the Bill of Rights were protected.
statements.context: Senate hearing on Artificial Intelligence in Government, Senator Paul questioning a witness on surveillance, rights, and disinformation.

statements.text: as much as I want to say, oh, let us all get together, we are going to hold hands and have transparency and fix the contracting in AI, I am more than worried than ever. I am not an opponent of AI. My son does AI. I am a fan of technology. I think AI can do great things.
statements.context: Senate hearing on governing AI through acquisition and procurement, featuring Senator Paul questioning witnesses about AI-driven content moderation and government speech suppression.

statements.text: Now I am supposed to trust DARPA with artificial intelligence, an agency that won't give me unclassified documents with proper request. That is a real danger that DARPA, Defense Threat Reduction Agency (DTRA), all these defense and intelligence agencies that are developing this to spy on others are so secretive that we don't have oversight.
statements.context: Senate hearing on governing AI through acquisition and procurement, where Senator Paul questions oversight of defense agencies developing AI.

statements.text: Our concern with artificial intelligence is they will take that tool and much more efficiently go through millions and millions opposed to say, that is not allowed. [...] It is amazing. This was no sort of please take down some information. It is, take it down or else.
statements.context: Senate hearing statement on AI acquisition and procurement, delivered by Senator Rand Paul.

statements.text: The PRC has waged an aggressive campaign to export its authoritarian model, including through its AI-driven surveillance technology, to countries across the Indo-Pacific and beyond. This campaign directly undermines U.S. national security interests and weakens human rights protections and institutions in the affected countries. [...] If confirmed, I will first review how the Administration is countering these actions by the PRC and other governments, particularly in reining in these repressive technologies. [...] working with allies and partners to ensure that dangerous technologies are not undermining a free, open, prosperous, and secure international order and working with interagency partners such as the Departments of Commerce and Treasury to leverage sanctions and other accountability tools, export controls, and other mechanisms to make progress.
statements.context: Written responses to Senate Foreign Relations Committee questions for the record during a nominations hearing for the 118th Congress, Second Session.

statements.venue: Interview with Privacy Daily on the proposed federal AI moratorium on state laws

statements.text: I think if you’re in a crowded area, a suburb of a big town, you say, ‘I may not want a whole power grid and a data center here,’ [...] If you live in a rural community that really is hungry for jobs and needs population, you might want one.
statements.venue: Press conference, reported by Kentucky Lantern

statements.text: You can’t just have data centers without energy, so we’re going to need more energy. [...] And it’s one of those things where I may weigh in with an opinion, but ultimately, most of that will be decided here.
statements.venue: Press conference, reported by Kentucky Lantern

statements.text: If Congress acts hastily before the technology is understood, Congress risks killing innovation and setting this technology back decades. [...] Think, for example, that your search engine that you already use today is AI. [...] Are they going to have to redesign all search engines immediately if this passes and put kill switches in your search engine?
statements.venue: Senate floor, objecting to Sen. Kennedy's AI kill switch bill (via Duke City Wire)

statements.text: AI is going to be throughout the economy and so many facets. Are doctors going to have to build a kill switch into drug prescription analysis?
statements.venue: Senate floor, objecting to Sen. Kennedy's AI kill switch bill (via Duke City Wire)

statements.text: I think we should make sure we have as many facts as possible before we dictate rules for the whole economy. Artificial intelligence is an incredible technology; it’s quickly transforming how work is done.
statements.venue: Senate floor remarks on AI kill switch bill (via Tampa Free Press)

statements.text: I don’t oppose the spirit of this bill, but I do ask that we make sure that we have all the information.
statements.venue: Senate floor remarks on AI kill switch bill (via news report)
